## Grammar

Basic word order is free (no basic order of subject, object and verb); it has prepositions. In the noun phrase: possessed before the possessor; noun before the adjective; demonstrative before the noun; noun before the numeral; noun before the relative clause. Overall it is head-initial.
It has no definite article, no indefinite article, no case marking on nouns, no alignment marking (subject and object are not told apart by form), singular and plural, no gender or noun classes.
Verbs mark past and future; there are no evidentials. Negation uses a negator before the verb; yes/no questions use intonation alone. Verbs do not agree with their arguments.
Other features: verb reduplication; adjectives that behave like verbs; a bound causative; a bound passive; question words moved to the front.
